description: On a runner with Docker and systemd. Exited containers: one OOM-killed (16 MiB limit, a shell that allocates) always alerts, worded as an out-of-memory kill; docker stop giving 143 (sleep behind --init) and 137 (a shell as PID 1 that ignores TERM) is named in the status under usrStoppedExitAction Warn and alerts under Alert; exit code 1 alerts as before; usrIncludeLogs Yes puts the last log lines in the diagnostic and says so in the status. Baseline age: saved state an hour old gives the restart-loop alert; made 7 hours old, the run takes a new baseline, raises no restart alert, resets breach streaks and says so. The state directory /var/lib/tc-docker: a symlink there is not followed and a directory not owned by root is not used (the check still runs and says the state was not saved, and why); a symlink at the state file is not read, written through or replaced. State an earlier version left in /var/lib/tc-docker-monitor is read once, when root's, and that directory is never changed or made again. usrExclude starting with - is a pattern. A docker shim that never answers (also one that ignores TERM, and one that hangs only docker stats) gives 'Docker did not answer within 60 seconds', exit 1, inside 90 seconds, nothing left running and a sibling in the caller's process group untouched. docker.service stopped with docker.socket listening: exit 0, no docker command run, Docker still stopped. No docker command but a socket: exit 1; a client only in /snap/bin is found through the appended PATH. GNU bash 4.2 runs the main paths without an unbound-variable crash. The first step reads the script itself: its time-limit functions sit in one block marked tc-docker bounded (a block CI compares with the other Docker monitors' copies), and its tc-docker running block says it is identical in every tc-docker component. Version 3: the result code is one block marked tc-docker result, shared with the other two Docker monitors (a step reads the script for it), and TERM mid-run gives one fallback result block, 'Check could not run: the monitor stopped unexpectedly'. The state file is written with tc_state_write, in the block marked tc-docker state, the same in the prune and the three Docker monitors (a step reads the script for it). The script's opening comment is short and points to the README (a step reads it).

steps.label: Test helpers: tc-test-run (runs the monitor the way the harness does, timed, under /bin/bash or bash 4.2), tc-test-left, tc-test-dstate, tc-test-state, tc-test-clean; a tiny local image tc-test-base:1; one running container tc-run1
steps.run:
set -e
M="$PWD/Monitors/docker-container-health-and-resource-usage-lin/docker-container-health-and-resource-usage-lin.sh"
test -f "$M"
cat > /usr/local/bin/tc-test-run <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# tc-test-run [--bash42] [VAR=value...]: run the monitor as the harness does (a clean
# environment and the agent's root PATH); print its output, exit code and seconds taken.
b=/bin/bash; if [ "${1:-}" = --bash42 ]; then b=/opt/tc-bash42/bin/bash; shift; fi
t0=$(date +%s)
env -i PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin HOME=/root "$@" "$b" "@MONITOR@"
rc=$?
secs=$(( $(date +%s) - t0 ))
echo "exit $rc after $secs seconds, under $("$b" -c 'echo "bash $BASH_VERSION"')"
[ "$secs" -lt 90 ] && echo "result inside 90 seconds"
exit 0
EOF
sed -i "s|@MONITOR@|$M|" /usr/local/bin/tc-test-run
cat > /usr/local/bin/tc-test-left <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# tc-test-left: any docker shim process still running, from ps.
sleep 1
echo "--- ps -eo pid,ppid,pgid,etime,args, docker shims and their children:"
ps -eo pid,ppid,pgid,etime,args | grep -E '[/]usr/local/sbin/docker|[s]leep 600|[t]c-test-shim' || echo "no docker client or shim process left"
EOF
cat > /usr/local/bin/tc-test-dstate <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# tc-test-dstate LABEL: what systemd says about Docker.
echo "$1: systemctl is-active docker.service docker.socket -> $(systemctl is-active docker.service docker.socket | paste -sd' ')"
EOF
cat > /usr/local/bin/tc-test-state <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# tc-test-state: the state directory and the state file, or that they are not there.
d=/var/lib/tc-docker; f=$d/monitor-state.tsv
ls -lad "$d" 2>&1
if [ -f "$f" ] && [ ! -L "$f" ]; then echo "--- $f (now $(date +%s)):"; ls -la "$f"; cat "$f"; else echo "(no state file)"; fi
EOF
cat > /usr/local/bin/tc-test-clean <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# tc-test-clean: remove every container except tc-run1, and the monitor's state.
for c in $(docker ps -aq --no-trunc); do
    [ "$(docker inspect -f '{{.Name}}' "$c")" = /tc-run1 ] || docker rm -f "$c" >/dev/null
done
rm -rf /var/lib/tc-docker /var/lib/tc-docker-monitor
docker ps -a --format '{{.Names}} {{.Status}}' | sort
EOF
chmod 755 /usr/local/bin/tc-test-run /usr/local/bin/tc-test-left /usr/local/bin/tc-test-dstate /usr/local/bin/tc-test-state /usr/local/bin/tc-test-clean
# A tiny image built here (sh, sleep, true and their libraries), so no registry is needed.
r=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p "$r/bin"
for b in /bin/sh /bin/sleep /bin/true; do
    cp "$(readlink -f "$b")" "$r/bin/$(basename "$b")"
    for l in $(ldd "$b" | grep -oE '/[^ ]+'); do mkdir -p "$r$(dirname "$l")"; cp -L "$l" "$r$l" 2>/dev/null || true; done
done
tar -C "$r" -c . | docker import - tc-test-base:1 >/dev/null; rm -rf "$r"
docker run --rm tc-test-base:1 /bin/sh -c 'echo "tc-test-base:1 runs"'
for c in $(docker ps -aq); do docker rm -f "$c" >/dev/null; done
rm -rf /var/lib/tc-docker /var/lib/tc-docker-monitor
docker run -d --name tc-run1 tc-test-base:1 /bin/sleep 86400 >/dev/null
echo "helpers installed for $M"

steps.label: bash 4.2: build GNU bash 4.2 from the GNU release (sha256 checked) into /opt/tc-bash42; it has the bug: an empty array is unbound under set -u
steps.run:
set -e
d=$(mktemp -d); cd "$d"
for u in https://ftp.gnu.org/gnu/bash/bash-4.2.tar.gz https://ftpmirror.gnu.org/bash/bash-4.2.tar.gz; do
  curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o bash-4.2.tar.gz "$u" && break
done
echo 'a27a1179ec9c0830c65c6aa5d7dab60f7ce1a2a608618570f96bfa72e95ab3d8  bash-4.2.tar.gz' | sha256sum -c -
tar xzf bash-4.2.tar.gz
cd bash-4.2
# 2011 C: -std=gnu89 goes in CC so it also reaches the build-time tools (CC_FOR_BUILD), which a
# newer gcc defaulting to C23 otherwise refuses; the old-style warnings stay warnings.
W='-O1 -fpermissive -Wno-implicit-function-declaration -Wno-implicit-int -Wno-int-conversion -Wno-incompatible-pointer-types -Wno-return-mismatch'
gcc --version | head -n 1
CC='gcc -std=gnu89' CFLAGS="$W" CFLAGS_FOR_BUILD="$W" ./configure --without-bash-malloc --disable-nls >configure.log 2>&1 || { tail -n 30 configure.log; exit 1; }
make -j"$(nproc)" >make.log 2>&1 || { grep -m 20 'error:' make.log; tail -n 30 make.log; exit 1; }
install -D -m 755 bash /opt/tc-bash42/bin/bash
/opt/tc-bash42/bin/bash -c 'echo "built bash $BASH_VERSION"'
/opt/tc-bash42/bin/bash -c 'set -u; a=(); echo "${a[@]}"' 2>&1 || true

steps.label: Hung daemon that ignores TERM: a shim that traps TERM and loops
steps.run: printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/sh' '# tc-test-shim: ignores TERM and never answers' "trap '' TERM" 'while :; do sleep 1; done' > /usr/local/sbin/docker; chmod 755 /usr/local/sbin/docker; cat /usr/local/sbin/docker

steps.label: A shim that ignores TERM: killed with what is left of its group; inside 90 seconds, nothing left
steps.run: tc-test-run; tc-test-left
outputContains: Docker did not answer within 60 seconds
no docker client or shim process left

steps.label: Hung stats: a shim that passes everything but docker stats to Docker
steps.run: real=$(cat /var/tmp/tc-docker-real); printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/sh' '# tc-test-shim: docker stats never answers' "[ \"\$1\" = stats ] && exec sleep 600" "exec $real \"\$@\"" > /usr/local/sbin/docker; chmod 755 /usr/local/sbin/docker; docker info --format 'docker info still answers: {{.ServerVersion}}'

steps.label: Hung stats: exit 1, and the diagnostic says it was docker stats
outputContains: STATUS=Check could not run: Docker did not answer within 60 seconds

steps.label: Hung stats: nothing left running
steps.run: tc-test-left
outputContains: no docker client or shim process left

steps.label: Shims removed: Docker answers again
steps.run: rm -f /usr/local/sbin/docker; hash -r; docker ps >/dev/null && echo 'docker ps answers again'

steps.label: Stopped Docker: a shim on PATH records any docker command; docker.service stopped while docker.socket keeps listening
steps.run: set -e; real=$(command -v docker); test "$real" != /usr/local/sbin/docker; printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/sh' '# tc-test-shim: records every docker command' 'echo "$*" >> /var/tmp/tc-docker-calls' "exec $real \"\$@\"" > /usr/local/sbin/docker; chmod 755 /usr/local/sbin/docker; hash -r; : > /var/tmp/tc-docker-calls; tc-test-dstate before; systemctl stop docker.service 2>/dev/null; tc-test-dstate stopped; echo "docker commands run: $(wc -l < /var/tmp/tc-docker-calls)"
outputContains: before: systemctl is-active docker.service docker.socket -> active active
stopped: systemctl is-active docker.service docker.socket -> inactive active

steps.label: Docker stopped: exit 0, says so, and runs no docker command
outputContains: STATUS=Docker is stopped (docker.service is inactive); nothing to check

steps.label: bash 4.2: Docker stopped
steps.run: tc-test-run --bash42
outputContains: STATUS=Docker is stopped (docker.service is inactive); nothing to check

steps.label: Stopped Docker: still stopped, and no docker command was run; then Docker started again, and tc-run1 with it
steps.run: tc-test-dstate after; echo "docker commands run: $(wc -l < /var/tmp/tc-docker-calls)"; rm -f /usr/local/sbin/docker /var/tmp/tc-docker-calls; hash -r; systemctl start docker.service; for i in $(seq 30); do docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; sleep 1; done; docker start tc-run1 >/dev/null; tc-test-dstate restarted
outputContains: after: systemctl is-active docker.service docker.socket -> inactive active
restarted: systemctl is-active docker.service docker.socket -> active active

steps.label: Docker answers again: healthy
No docker command, but Docker's socket is there: the client moved out of every PATH directory
steps.run: set -e; real=$(command -v docker); echo "$real" > /var/tmp/tc-docker-real; mv "$real" /var/tmp/tc-docker-cli.moved; hash -r; command -v docker || echo 'no docker command'; test -S /var/run/docker.sock && echo '/var/run/docker.sock is a socket'

steps.label: Socket present, no docker command: exit 1
outputContains: STATUS=Docker appears to be installed but no docker command was found

steps.label: PATH: the docker client in /snap/bin only, which the harness PATH does not reach and the monitor's appended PATH does
steps.run: set -e; mkdir -p /snap/bin; mv /var/tmp/tc-docker-cli.moved /snap/bin/docker; env -i PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin /bin/bash -c 'command -v docker || echo "not on the harness PATH"'

steps.label: Docker only on the appended PATH: found, and the check runs as usual
PATH: the client put back where it was
steps.run: set -e; mv /snap/bin/docker "$(cat /var/tmp/tc-docker-real)"; rm -f /var/tmp/tc-docker-real; hash -r; docker ps --format '{{.Names}}'

steps.label: Back to normal
